findings.title: Keep the learner gloss aligned with supported current usage
findings.details: A review rejected “up” in the learner overview because its citations supported current “above/upper side,” while upward-motion examples were only historical reports. A later revision passed using “above” or “upper.” Preserve that distinction when revising the learner account.
findings.verification: Check that the learner overview uses a current-use gloss supported by E4 and E7, and does not present historically reported upward-motion glosses as current without current-use evidence.

findings.title: Preserve the qualified disagreement over the early reference line
findings.details: Accounts agree on an early mark above a reference line but differ on whether that line was curved or horizontal; no primary inscription image was inspected to settle the variation. Reviews rejected learner wording that treated the interpretation as settled. Keep the proposal qualified and the disagreement distinct from the present graph’s dot above a horizontal stroke.
findings.verification: Check learner and expert prose against cited accounts, retain the curved-versus-horizontal qualification, identify the exact graph being described, and do not imply the modern strokes prove the ancient analysis.

findings.title: Keep sense status and dating tied to the evidence
findings.details: Reviews required separating current-use support from historical examples, narrowing the spatial sense’s period to the reported Zhou bronze contexts, and not treating Shang compound contexts such as 上帝 and 上甲 as attestation of the single-character sense “above.” They also required historical-relationship claims to cite evidence that addresses chronology. The final article passed factual review, but these are material recurring checks for this entry.
findings.verification: For each sense, verify that current status has present-use evidence, period wording matches the cited attestation, compound contexts are not treated as single-character uses, and chronology claims cite evidence that addresses the relationship.

findings.title: Describe the curated seal-style rendering accurately
findings.details: A review found that the caption incorrectly treated the rendering’s upper stroke as separate from the central upright. The corrected caption describes the visible long baseline, central upright, and upper stroke bending right and descending into it, while retaining qualified seal-style provenance.
findings.verification: Compare the caption and alt text with the attached rendering; confirm the upper stroke is described as joining the upright and that the redraw is not presented as a dated artifact.

findings.title: Record the inaccessible Unihan endpoint in the 上 research
findings.details: The research audit reports that the character-specific Unicode Unihan endpoint for 上 was inaccessible. The local kMandarin row gives shàng, while CNS11643 independently lists readings; the local row should not be described as verified through the failed endpoint.
findings.verification: If citing or relying on the Unicode endpoint, obtain an accessible character-specific record and verify its contents; otherwise retain the access gap and distinguish local data from independently inspected sources.
